propositions: The reconciler's baseline snapshot is advanced from the pass-start fetch before outbound apply, so when rebar itself pushes a status change to Jira, the baseline retains the old value for one pass, causing a false local==baseline match that suppresses the outbound reopen and allows inbound to clobber it.

A local status change that equals the stale baseline is suppressed from outbound because _suppressed_by_inbound interprets local==baseline as 'local unchanged since sync', but the baseline lags rebar's own write by one pass, making that premise false.

The same ABA exposure affects all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) because all share the _suppressed_by_inbound guard, so a soft-failed mutation must gate baseline advance on per-call success, not pass exit code.

A soft-failed status transition (unreachable transition or 400 comment-fallback) allows the pass to exit 0 while the push never landed, so advancing the baseline for a failed mutation would falsely record a sync and mask divergence.

Option A fixes the defect by overlaying successfully-applied outbound values onto the pass-start snapshot before baseline advance, restoring ADR 0026's last-synced definition, and gating the overlay on per-mutation success via new return-value plumbing through dispatch_one, apply_handlers, and applier.

The direction-preservation regression cell for status existed only on an unused code path (_diff_fields with no production caller) before this fix; new cells on the live diff_canonical_fields path for all five mirrored fields, with explicit reachability assertions, prevent the tests from passing by not running.
